subject: Human Body
title: Adrenaline: Fight or Flight
description: Learn Adrenaline: Fight or Flight in one minute.

hook.text: A car swerves toward you. In milliseconds, adrenaline floods your body. Heart races, pupils dilate, muscles tense.

buildup.text: Adrenaline (epinephrine) is released by the adrenal medulla. It prepares the body to fight or flee a perceived threat.

discovery.text: It diverts blood from digestion to muscles, increases breathing rate, and releases stored glucose for explosive energy.

twist.text: Panic attacks trigger adrenaline without real danger. The body can't tell the difference between a tiger and anxiety.

climax.text: Adrenaline evolved for emergencies. It supercharges the body for seconds to minutes — long enough to survive or escape.

punchline.text: Adrenaline turns your body into an emergency machine. Instantly.

quiz.question: Why can panic attacks feel physically identical to real danger?
options: The brain produces a different stress hormone
The body releases adrenaline regardless of whether the threat is real
Panic attacks only affect the mind, not the body
